subjects.subject: English Language
subjects.name: Basic 3 English Language
subjects.description: The Basic 3 English Language curriculum deepens the development of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. It emphasizes oral language competence through storytelling, conversation, and presentation, while advancing reading proficiency with phonics, vocabulary, and comprehension strategies.

strands.title: Oral Language (Listening and Speaking)
strands.description: Developing advanced listening and speaking skills through songs, rhymes, storytelling, dramatisation, conversation, and presentation.

subStrands.title: Songs
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding of a variety of songs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of a variety of songs

indicators.description: Talk about the benefits of songs

exemplars.description: Let learners identify some familiar songs e.g. patriotic songs such as 'The National Anthem'.
Teach the songs identified, e. g. 'The National Anthem'
Let learners sing rhythmically, using claps, gestures and dance where necessary.
Let learners, in convenient groups, identify and talk about the moral lessons in the songs.
Have learners think-pair-share the benefits of songs. Let the pairs then share their views with the whole class.

subStrands.title: Rhymes
subStrands.description: Appreciating a variety of literary pieces through rhymes.

contentStandards.description: Appreciate a variety of literary pieces

indicators.description: Compose short rhymes and tongue-twisters and recite them

exemplars.description: Revise some previously taught rhymes.
Present the new rhymes and perform them as learners listen and observe.
Read through the lines meaningfully with learners.
Let learners read through the lines in groups and individually on their own.
Focus on rhyming words by helping learners to identify them.
Put learners in convenient groups. Assign them a rhyme and task them to compose a parallel one.
Have groups recite their rhymes with the class.

subStrands.title: Story Telling
subStrands.description: Responding to stories and creating own stories.

contentStandards.description: Respond to stories

indicators.description: Respond to and ask questions based on stories heard

exemplars.description: Select a suitable story to tell or read to the class. e.g. Ananse and the family.
Let learners tell their favourite parts of the story.
Have learners respond to the story by asking and answering relevant questions to enhance comprehension.

indicators.description: Tell parallel stories

exemplars.description: Select a suitable story to tell or read to learners, e.g. The old man.
Put learners into groups to compose a parallel story.
Let learners present their stories to the class for feedback.

indicators.description: Create own events to extend stories heard

exemplars.description: Let learners retell some stories they have read or heard. e.g. Ananse and the wisdom pot.
Pair up learners and have them create their own events to extend a story of their choice.
Invite representatives of the groups to share the part of the story they have created with the class.

subStrands.title: Dramatisation and Role Play
subStrands.description: Performing stories through dramatisation.

contentStandards.description: Perform stories

indicators.description: Dramatise and role-play stories heard and read

exemplars.description: Let learners mention titles of stories they have heard or read, e.g. The Magic Pot.
Let learners identify some characters in the stories mentioned.
Let learners dramatise or role-play stories they have heard, read or created, with appropriate characters.
Discuss stories dramatised or role-played.
Let learners comment on stories dramatised or role-played.

subStrands.title: Conversation
subStrands.description: Talking about Oneself, Family, People, Places, Greetings, Customs, Events, Social/Cultural Values, Manners and other Themes.

contentStandards.description: Explore using certain culturally acceptable language for communication

indicators.description: Use appropriate greetings for special occasions

exemplars.description: Revise greetings for special occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries, festivals.
Let learners take turns to demonstrate greetings for special occasions and practise the appropriate responses.
Put learners into groups. Assign each group a special occasion for them to practise greetings and responses for that occasion.

indicators.description: Talk about events in the community

exemplars.description: Have learners sing a familiar song about a topic.
Show pictures of events in the community, e.g. durbar, festival, naming ceremony, birthday.
Have learners think-pair-share the events with the person sitting next to them.
Have the pairs share their experiences with the class.
Have learners talk about which of the events they like most and why they like them.
Let learners, in groups, role-play the events of their choice.

indicators.description: Talk about important places in their communities

exemplars.description: Show pictures of important places in their communities such as the community centre, the lorry station, the mission house, the market, the fire service station etc.
Let learners think-pair-share their views and opinions about the pictures.
Put learners into groups according to the number of pictures.
Have each group talk about the activities that go on in these places and their importance to the community and the nation.

indicators.description: Use a wider variety of words to talk about different customs and cultural values

exemplars.description: Using conversational posters on different customs and cultural practices, let learners think-pair-share, looking at the various illustrations on the poster.
Have them use expressions learnt and other new ones to talk about the customs and cultural practices.
Let learners, in groups, role-play the customs and cultural practices on the poster.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of language and communicative skills to participate in conversation

indicators.description: Demonstrate turn-taking in conversation in different topics

exemplars.description: Let learners identify some familiar/interesting topics based on their environment for discussion.eg. Sanitation, Bush fires, Flooding, Pollution.
Let learners give scenarios from the identified topics.
Let learners demonstrate taking turns in conversations.
Guide appropriate language use in conversation.

indicators.description: Ask and answer questions for clarification about what other people say

exemplars.description: Revise topics previously discussed, e.g. Climate Change.
Ask questions on the topic discussed.
Let learners answer questions based on the topic discussed.
Guide and encourage learners to ask and answer questions for clarification on what other learners say.

indicators.description: Participate in communication, using more varied and more accurate language

exemplars.description: Put learners in groups. Have each group discuss the conversation posters on issues such as situations, events, customs, etc.

indicators.description: Express a greater variety of communicative meaning (e.g. apologising, agreeing or disagreeing)

exemplars.description: Let learners role-play topics or themes discussed.
Discuss the importance of expressing a variety of communicative meanings/telling people about their feelings, etc.) e. g. apologising, agreeing or disagreeing with partners on issues.
Guide learners to express a variety of communicative meanings.

subStrands.title: Listening Comprehension
subStrands.description: Using skills and strategies to process meaning from texts.

contentStandards.description: Use appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts

indicators.description: Listen to and interact actively within information texts

exemplars.description: Note: For all information text, use the KWL strategy. Below is the process: Before reading, let learners think- pair- share, and talk about what they already know (K) about the topic Have learners ask questions about what they want to know (W).
While you read the text, pause often to give the children the chance to share what they have learned
Let learners answer the questions they asked before reading.
After the reading, have learners share what they have learned.

indicators.description: Recognise and relate the sequence of events in stories

exemplars.description: Read a narrative text aloud to learners.
Put learners in groups to identify and talk about the parts of the story (e.g. beginning, middle and end).

indicators.description: Share facts from information texts heard with a partner, groups or the teacher

exemplars.description: Read an information text aloud to learners using the KWL Strategy. KWL Strategy: Before reading, have learners think-pair-share and talk about what they already know (K) about the title of the text. Have learners ask questions about what they want to know. (W).
While you read the text, pause often to give the children the chance to share what they have learned or answer the questions they have asked before reading.
After the reading, have learners share what they have learned.
Put learners in groups to share facts from the text heard.

subStrands.title: Asking and Answering Questions
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in asking and answering questions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in asking and answering questions

indicators.description: Ask and answer questions for clarifications about given topics

exemplars.description: Let learners select topics of interest for discussion.
Put learners in groups and have them ballot for topics.
Let members of each group discuss topics respecting rules of conversation.
Encourage learners to ask and answer questions for clarifications on issues raised in their discussion.

indicators.description: Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering the inversion questions

exemplars.description: Let learners, in pairs, ask and answer questions on given issues.
Revise inversion questions with learners. e. g. He is going. Is he going?
Guide learners to use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering the inversion type of questions.
Let learners write answers to inversion type of questions on their own.

subStrands.title: Giving and Responding to Commands, Instructions, Directions and Making Requests
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests

indicators.description: Give and respond to commands, instructions and directions

exemplars.description: A. Instructions: Model giving instructions and ask learners to follow them: First, draw a square in the middle of your paper. Next, draw a rectangle inside the square. Then, draw an oval inside the rectangle. Response: [Learners draw according to instructions]. Pair up learners to practise giving and following instructions, e.g. giving and following instructions to clean the classroom.

B. Directions: Model giving directions and ask learners to follow them: Show directions flash cards (go straight, turn left/right) and ensure learners understand the words. Place objects at different locations of the classroom. Ask questions such as "Where is the book, pen, bag etc.? Then show the direction flash cards to help learners locate the items. Invite pairs of learners to practise giving and following directions. They can locate objects and places in the school.

indicators.description: Make and respond to polite requests

exemplars.description: Show pictures of requests to learners and ask them to guess the requests from pictures: e.g. a picture of a closed door, a picture of an open door, a picture of someone carrying books etc. (Can you help me carry the books?, Please, close/open the door.)
Invite pairs of learners to the front of the class to make and respond to polite requests. Let learner A pick a picture and Learner B make the request. Then, Learner A responds to the request made.
Have learners draw pictures of requests for their partners to guess the requests.
Let learners practise making and accepting or declining requests using expressions such as "Yes, Of course, No problem, I'm sorry, I can't, etc."

subStrands.title: Presentation
subStrands.description: Planning and presenting information and ideas for a variety of purposes.

contentStandards.description: Plan and present information and ideas for a variety of purposes

indicators.description: Present ideas logically

exemplars.description: Discuss important people (e.g. teachers, footballers, farmer, police officer, etc.) in learners' community and what made them important.
Ask learners to prepare presentations on what they would like to be important for and why.
Have learners present their work logically.

indicators.description: Use appropriate verbal and non-verbal cues to convey meaning while speaking, e.g. smiling, using gestures, etc

exemplars.description: Demonstrate use of appropriate posture, verbal and non-verbal cues to communicate meaning, e.g. nodding, smiling, etc. to show approval.
Discuss the various non-verbal cues (e.g. facial expression, eye contact, crossed arms, etc.) you used and their meanings with learners.
Let the groups plan their presentations on an appropriate topic.
Give each group time to present and have the class talk about the appropriate verbal and non-verbal cues used.

strands.title: Reading
strands.description: Developing reading skills through phonics, word families, vocabulary, comprehension, and fluency.

subStrands.title: Phonics
subStrands.description: Connecting sounds to letters and blending them to read and write.

contentStandards.description: Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write

indicators.description: Understand the relationship between spelling of words and sounds of speech

exemplars.description: Have learners revise writing out some words as you pronounce them. (You can also make them read words on the board or word cards).
Provide activities for learners to use letter names and sounds to spell and sound out words.

indicators.description: Use the alphabetic knowledge to decode unknown words (e.g. consonant blends, consonant digraphs, vowel sounds, vowel diagraphs and word patterns)

exemplars.description: Have learners sing an alphabet song.

Introduce consonant blends and digraphs, one at a time and have learners form words out of them and use them in sentences. Note: An important thing to remember is that a digraph is made of two letters, although the letters spell a sound e.g. bl, br, ch, ck, cl, cr, dr, fl, fr, gh, gl
Use the same procedure to teach vowel digraphs e. g. ai, ee, ea, ie, ei, oo, oe, oo, ue, oi, au

indicators.description: Use basic elements of structural analysis (e.g prefixes, suffixes, compound, root words) to decode unknown words

exemplars.description: Guide learners with examples to use the structure of words to decode.
Introduce words and have learners look for the parts. e.g. syllables, prefixes and suffixes.
Let learners identify words with similar parts/structures.

subStrands.title: Word Families-Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs
subStrands.description: Using rhyming endings and digraphs to enhance reading comprehension.

contentStandards.description: Employ knowledge of rhyming endings and common digraphs to enhance reading comprehension

indicators.description: Use common rhyming/endings words for decoding of words

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to simple word formation by changing the beginning letter. e.g. pin, sin, fin
Have learners build on these rhyming endings and read out the words to their group members.
Have learners form sentences with these rhyming words.

indicators.description: Use words containing digraphs to make meaningful sentences

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to simple digraphs as in: sh- shirt, ch- church, gh- Ghana, ph-phone
Have learners build as many words as possible with the digraphs and form meaningful sentences with some of the words.

subStrands.title: Diphthongs
subStrands.description: Understanding and using diphthongs.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of diphthongs

indicators.description: Use diphthongs to build words

exemplars.description: Revise digraphs and have learners identify them in words.
Introduce diphthongs in context. e.g. ou-out, loud, cloud
Through think-pair-share, let learners generate diphthongs and build words with them.

subStrands.title: Blends and Consonant Clusters
subStrands.description: Identifying and using consonant blends.

contentStandards.description: Identify and use consonant blends in words

indicators.description: Use consonant blends to build words

exemplars.description: Have learners revise diphthongs and use them in sentences.
Introduce consonant blends and have learners identify words having the blends. e.g. bl - black, br- brush, st- stone, tr- tree
Let learners work in pairs/groups to identify consonant blends and build words from them.

subStrands.title: Vocabulary
subStrands.description: Understanding word meanings and usages.

contentStandards.description: Understand word meanings and usage

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate sight words, understand and use them in meaningful complex sentences

exemplars.description: Provide learners with texts containing level-appropriate sight words.
Put them into groups to identify, read and use sight words in meaningful sentences.

indicators.description: Use knowledge of prefixes and suffixes to interpret unfamiliar words
Understand and use many of the frequently occurring words and chunks in the language, including both content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs) and function words ( prepositions, articles)

exemplars.description: Revise learners RPK by asking them to use some sight words learnt in earlier lessons.
Introduce new words and have learners form sentences with them as you guide them with simple ways to find contextual meanings of words.
You may introduce game activities e.g. Lucky Dip to provide practice in identification and use of sight words.

indicators.description: Use dictionaries, glossaries and internet to clarify word meanings

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to the dictionary and glossaries.
Have learners find the dictionary meaning to key words in a comprehension passage.
Have learners make or build their own glossaries on the words learnt.
In groups, let learners practise finding key words and building their own word albums/dictionaries/glossaries.

subStrands.title: Comprehension
subStrands.description: Understanding and analysing texts read.

contentStandards.description: Understand and analyse texts read

indicators.description: Use self-correction strategies to make meaning when reading texts

exemplars.description: Engage learners on before reading activities, e.g. review of background knowledge, discussion of title and accompanying pictures).
Model reading the text aloud and have learners echo-read the text (if necessary).
Read out words and sentences for learners to identify in the text.
Let learners read aloud in groups and pairs and answer questions.

indicators.description: Ask and answer factual, inferential and vocabulary questions about level-appropriate texts

exemplars.description: Have learners brainstorm on the topic on which they will answer questions.
Ask learners to read and answer simple pre-reading questions as you guide them.
Guide learners to ask and answer factual, inferential and vocabulary questions on the passage read.

indicators.description: Retell level-appropriate text in own, explain and illustrate

exemplars.description: Ask a few questions to review the text/story to be retold.
Have learners narrate or retell the story passage using the herring bone or story map strategy. The narration should be sequential to make the story understood.

contentStandards.description: Use knowledge, skills and techniques of reading to understand, interpret and appreciate a variety of literary texts

indicators.description: Demonstrate understanding of the purpose and features of poems or rhymes and fables, etc

exemplars.description: Introduce the lesson with before reading activities, singing, reciting, prediction, etc.
Have learners read a text and identify its purpose and features. Guide them with questions to do this.
Let learners transfer the same ideas to other types of texts.
Use think-pair-share to have learners compare ideas.

indicators.description: Respond to stories with own opinion and value judgment

exemplars.description: Have learners give their personal opinions and judgment to stories (events, setting, characters and their actions) read or heard.

indicators.description: Use visualisation strategy (form mental images when reading text) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts

exemplars.description: Have learners play simple mental or guessing games like Bingo and matching games.
Guide learners to form mental images as they read a text, to help them make meaning from the text.

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate texts independently

exemplars.description: Provide learners with level-appropriate texts and encourage them to read independently.
Let learners may be provided with pre-reading questions to enable them focus.

subStrands.title: Fluency
subStrands.description: Reading texts with good speed, accuracy, and expression.

contentStandards.description: Read texts fluently

indicators.description: Read long texts with good pace, accuracy and expression

exemplars.description: Engage learners in pre-reading and demonstrate/model reading aloud with fluency, accuracy and expression.
Have learners practise in pairs and groups. Note: Learners must read at their own pace.

indicators.description: Recognise more than two hundred high frequency words with automaticity

exemplars.description: Revise the knowledge of sight words through games.
Have learners identify sight words in texts using games such as Fishing and Lucky Dip.
Let learners use the sight words to construct meaningful sentences.

indicators.description: Use self-correction strategy to make meaning from texts (repeated)

exemplars.description: Have learners use self-correction strategy as they pronounce words in a read aloud lesson.
Check for intonation and pace as they read to make meaning.

strands.title: Writing
strands.description: Developing writing skills through penmanship, labelling, sentence construction, composition, and writing as a process.

subStrands.title: Penmanship/Handwriting
subStrands.description: Copying and writing sentences correctly.

contentStandards.description: Copy and write sentences correctly

indicators.description: Copy short paragraphs clearly

exemplars.description: Model copying a short paragraph on the board drawing attention to features such as clarity, spacing and alignment of letters.
Let learners practise copying a short paragraph legibly and correctly on the board.
Have learners copy short paragraphs from a book into their exercise books.

subStrands.title: Writing /Copying Letters – Small and Capital
subStrands.description: Using letter-sound relationships to write legibly.

contentStandards.description: Use general skills, strategies and knowledge of letter sounds to write legibly and boldly

indicators.description: Use letter-sound relationships to represent most letters in words correctly

exemplars.description: Let learners play the alphabet sound game.
Dictate words and simple sentences for learners to write.

subStrands.title: Labelling items
subStrands.description: Making lists and labelling objects in the environment.

contentStandards.description: Draw and label simple pictures

indicators.description: Make a list of objects found in the environment

exemplars.description: Lead the class to make a list of objects found in a given thematic area. e.g. The Bus Stop.
Let groups and pairs make similar lists from self-chosen or given areas. They may use invented spelling initially.
Guide learners to edit and self-correct the errors before presenting their work to the class. They may use children’s pictures, dictionaries and other sources.

subStrands.title: Writing Simple Words and Sentences
subStrands.description: Writing accurately using acquired vocabulary and grammar.

contentStandards.description: Write accurately using acquired vocabulary and knowledge of grammar

indicators.description: Write simple sentences to express personal opinions about favourite characters in texts

exemplars.description: Put learners in groups to discuss characters in a story read.
Have learners write simple sentences to express personal opinions on favourite characters.

Let learners exchange their books and do peer editing by checking for: i. correct spelling of words, ii. correct writing of capitals, iii. correct writing of small letters, iv. correct spacing of letters and words.

indicators.description: Write simple meaningful sentences to express feelings and opinions about people and things

exemplars.description: Guide learners, with examples, to write simple sentences to express their feelings and opinions about their peers and things found in the environment.
Have the groups edit their work and publish them.

indicators.description: Draw pictures and write, at least, three sentences to share an opinion

exemplars.description: Show the images/‘smileys’ on a mobile phone.
Working in groups, let learners use the computer to search for these smiley/images. (The ICT teacher can guide learners by showing the appropriate icon to help them explore these).

Have learners draw their own pictures and write sentences to explain them. e.g. a drawing showing fruits can have a sentence such as “Eat fruits every day; Fruits have vitamin C; Fruits protect your body.”
Guide learners to do self and peer editing (The products can be transferred on to a manila card and posted on the walls in the classroom) to be appreciated and critiqued.

indicators.description: Copy various sentences, verses and words of songs legibly (writing should be bold and clear)

exemplars.description: Explain the writing activity selected, stressing the need for accuracy, clarity, etc.
As learners observe, demonstrate it.
Assign them to do the exercise. They may copy from the board and books.
Provide feedback after assessing learners’ work.

subStrands.title: Guided Composition
subStrands.description: Composing short paragraphs through answering questions.

contentStandards.description: Compose short paragraphs through answering questions

indicators.description: Develop two coherent paragraphs on one idea or concept using leading questions

exemplars.description: Have learners brainstorm to choose a topic, e. g. My home
Write the topic on the board.
Ask questions for learners to generate ideas on the topic
Discuss the questions with learners for them to answer appropriately e.g. My home i. Where do you live? ii. How many of you live there? iii. What kind of buildings are there?

subStrands.title: Writing as a Process
subStrands.description: Applying skills for idea generation, drafting, revising, and publishing.

contentStandards.description: Apply the skills and strategies for idea generation, selection, development, organization and revision in writing

indicators.description: Select a topic on familiar themes (e.g. Myself), brainstorm and organise before writing

exemplars.description: Take learners through the writing process: Pre-writing stage. Consider composition writing as a process. That is, it should be done in stages. Take learners through stages such as preparation, writing, editing and publishing.
Assist learners to prepare for writing by discussing the topic to write on, e.g. My school.
In groups, let learners discuss their ideas.
Use learner strategies such as brainstorming to help learners generate ideas appropriate to the topic.

contentStandards.description: Develop and express ideas coherently and cohesively in writing

indicators.description: Write ideas on a topic in simple sentences

exemplars.description: Writing stage: Have learners write their first draft in groups.
Let learners write their ideas as they appear, without taking particular note of corrections or editing.
Let learners add on new ideas that occur to them as they write.

contentStandards.description: Apply strategies for improving drafts for publishing

indicators.description: Review and revise the draft, adding to or taking out ideas

exemplars.description: In groups, have learners revise their writing paying attention to little details.

Have learners use these questions as a revision guide: i. Is my topic interesting? ii. Does the beginning catch the reader’s attention? iii. Are the ideas easy to understand? iv. Are all the sentences saying something about the topic?
Encourage learners to make as many changes as necessary to improve their work.

indicators.description: Proofread draft to correct punctuation and spelling errors

exemplars.description: Have learners proofread the revised draft of their writing for errors relating to the conventions of punctuation, capitalization, spelling, etc.
Have learners check their editing through CUPS: C- Capitalisation, U- language Usage, P- Punctuation, S- Spelling
Let learners do peer editing: learners check their partners’ writing for punctuation and spelling errors.
Have learners write a neat final copy and read it once again to check for errors.

indicators.description: Read aloud own writing to a group or whole class

exemplars.description: Have learners publish their work by showing it to others in small groups or in pairs or posting it on the class or school notice board for others to view.

subStrands.title: Narrative Writing
subStrands.description: Narrating situations, expressing feelings, and conveying points of view.

contentStandards.description: Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the world/fictional world

indicators.description: Add more details of a story structure to narrative stories, for example setting, characters, problem and resolution of the problem

exemplars.description: Read a short narrative story to learners; concentrate on the setting and the characters.
Let learners narrate their experiences.
Assist learners to pick a topic. e. g. The traffic light.

Let learners write on the topic, narrating their experience. E.g. On my way to school, I crossed the road. I looked left, right and left again. There was no vehicle coming. Then I walked quickly across the road.

indicators.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and introducing a narrative

exemplars.description: Narrate a story stressing the setting and the characters for learners to listen.
Let learners re-tell the story. They may do so in a chain.
Let learners create and write their own stories.

subStrands.title: Descriptive Writing
subStrands.description: Describing places and personal experiences.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of description of writing

indicators.description: Describe places in a coherent paragraph

exemplars.description: Have learners recall periods, times or moments that they had been happy or sad.
Discuss personal experiences with learners.
Guide them to state categorically some personal experiences they have encountered in their lives.
Have learners share their experiences using simple descriptive words.
Discuss lessons learnt from the experiences shared.
Have learners write experiences shared logically and sequentially. e.g. about interesting places they have visited.

subStrands.title: Persuasive/Argumentative Writing
subStrands.description: Supporting opinions with clear reasons.

contentStandards.description: Support an opinion in writing

indicators.description: Write a short paragraph to support an opinion or claims with clear reasons

exemplars.description: Choose a simple topic for an argument. e.g. Which food is better; rice or fufu? (It could be any food, depending on learners’ background.)
Let learners choose one of the meals and give reasons why they think it is better.
Put the class into two to argue on the topic.

subStrands.title: Informative/ Academic Writing
subStrands.description: Writing about events and presenting information.

contentStandards.description: Write on the events of the day

indicators.description: Write picture events using simple sentences

exemplars.description: Using dictionaries and modelling, guide learners to give information on events of the day to their partners, class /groups/partners.
Have learners represent this in the form of a picture.
Have learners write simple sentences to accompany the pictures.
Have learners share their work with the class. Note: (Give room for positive appreciation).

indicators.description: Make a radio/TV presentations/performances

exemplars.description: Let Learners rehearse presenting information on radio or TV.
Have learners generate ideas, plan and present them in groups as done on radio.
Assign groups to present their ideas to the whole class.
Plan for a live presentation/performance.

strands.title: Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage
strands.description: Applying grammar rules and conventions in writing and communication.

subStrands.title: Using Capitalisation
subStrands.description: Using capital letters correctly in writing.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of capitalisation in writing

indicators.description: Use capital letters to write initials and abbreviations

exemplars.description: Introduce initials and abbreviations in context.
Provide learners with sentences or texts containing initials and abbreviations for them to identify. e. g. WHO – World Health Organisation; K. S. Manu – Kofi Sakyi Manu
Give texts having full names of people and organisations.
Ask learners to rewrite the text and replace the full names of people and organisations with initials and abbreviations.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the ability to capitalise titles of texts

exemplars.description: Provide sample varied stories and passages whose titles or headings have capital letters at the beginning of content words, e.g. “Ananse and the Wisdom Pot".
Put learners into groups to study the titles/headings and discover the use of capital letters in context.
Have groups present their observations.
Give learners titles/headings of stories or texts in lower case for them to re-write using capital letters at the beginning of content words.

subStrands.title: Using Punctuation
subStrands.description: Applying punctuation marks in writing.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of the use of punctuation in communication

indicators.description: Use full stops in initials and abbreviations

exemplars.description: Revise the use of the full stop (.).
Provide a short passage of about four sentences.
Pair learners place a full stop at the end of each sentence.
Introduce full stops in initials and abbreviations. e.g. Mr. Badu - Mister Badu, A. O. Boateng – Adom Opoku Boateng
Provide opportunities for learners to practise using full stops in initials of their names, and abbreviations.

indicators.description: Use commas appropriately to list items

exemplars.description: Help learners to separate items in a list, using commas, e.g. My friend has a pen, pencil, eraser and a book.

indicators.description: Identify and use the apostrophe to show possession

exemplars.description: Introduce the apostrophe showing possession in context. e.g. Kofi's mother has travelled.

subStrands.title: Using Action Words
subStrands.description: Using verbs to express actions and states.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of action words in communication

indicators.description: Identify the present continuous form of action words in spoken and written communication

exemplars.description: Through demonstration, assist learners to use the continuous form of the action words such as running, eating and sitting. Provide sentences and let learners identify the continuous form of the action words: e.g. Adongo is running with the ball.

indicators.description: Use the present continuous form of verbs to describe actions taking place at the time of speaking

exemplars.description: Through examples, assist learners to use the continuous forms of action words in sentences. e.g. Aba is singing. They are jumping.
Present action pictures for learners to write simple sentences about the actions taking place.

indicators.description: Use simple past and the past continuous forms of verbs to express past actions

exemplars.description: Revise the use of the present simple and present continuous tenses.
Introduce the new form, one at a time, using examples and situations.
Provide examples for practice through drills and creation of situations.

subStrands.title: Using Qualifying Words –Adjectives
subStrands.description: Using adjectives to describe people and things.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of adjectives in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use adjectives in short sentences to describe height, length, etc

exemplars.description: Provide sentences with simple adjectives for learners to identify, e.g. I saw a tall tree.
Put learners in groups to use the adjectives identified in simple sentences.

subStrands.title: Using Qualifying Words – Adverbs
subStrands.description: Using adverbs to modify verbs.

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of adverbs in communication

indicators.description: Identify qualifying words

exemplars.description: Provide sentences with simple adverbs for learners to identify. e.g. i. He walked quickly to the church. ii. She danced beautifully.
Elicit other adverbs and provide practice.

indicators.description: Use adverbs correctly to express time, frequency, etc.

exemplars.description: Guide learners with examples and situations to use adverbs of time and frequency.

subStrands.title: Using Simple Prepositions
subStrands.description: Using prepositions to indicate direction and means.

contentStandards.description: Apply the knowledge of simple prepositions in oral and written communication

indicators.description: Identify prepositions in sentences to indicate directions and means, e.g. by bus

exemplars.description: Provide sample sentences. e.g. means -We are going home by bus. direction - The monkey is climbing up the tree.
Guide learners to discover the meaning of the sentences.
Draw learners’ attention to the words as prepositions.
Have learners complete sentences with given prepositions that indicate means and direction. e.g. Mr. Badu is travelling ________ train.

subStrands.title: Using Simple and Compound Sentences
subStrands.description: Understanding compound sentences.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of compound sentences in writing

indicators.description: Identify and use coordinating conjunctions to join similar ideas or contrasting ideas in sentences

exemplars.description: Demonstrate the structure of a compound sentence by joining simple sentences with and. e.g. The boy woke up. The boy prayed. + And -> The boy woke up and prayed.
Have learners identify the coordinating conjunction in the sentence.
Put learners in groups to form simple sentences.
Have groups join the simple sentences with and and but.

subStrands.title: Spelling
subStrands.description: Using phonics to spell words.

contentStandards.description: Use phonics knowledge to spell words

indicators.description: Spell phonically irregular words correctly

exemplars.description: Have learners play the Pick and Spell game to spell phonically irregular words. e. g. enough, answer, because, bought.
Dictate the words for learners to spell.
Have learners use these words in oral and written sentences.

Provide sentences with blank spaces for learners to fill in the blanks using the words they have learnt to spell. e.g. bought, answer, because, enough etc. ii. I drink ------- water. iii. Your ................. is wrong. iv. I miss the class ..................... I was late. v. My father ................... chocolate.

strands.title: Extensive Reading
strands.description: Building a culture of reading for pleasure and information.

subStrands.title: Building the Love and Culture of Reading
subStrands.description: Encouraging independent reading habits.

contentStandards.description: Read widely for pleasure and demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area

indicators.description: Read a variety of age and level-appropriate books and summarise them

exemplars.description: Using the Author’s chair, introduce the reading/library time.
Have a variety of age/level-appropriate books for learners to make a choice from.
Introduce narratives, expository, procedural texts to learners.
Guide learners to select books for readings.
